One IPv4 entry: pfb_create_suppression_file() writes it as it is.
Several IPv4 entries, one per line, in order.
Entries with a comment after #, blank lines, whole-line comments and CRLF line ends: the file holds the entries only, comments cut.
A repeated entry (also in another case): the file keeps both lines, Core lists it once.
The lowest mask the IP page accepts for IPv4, /8.
The highest mask, /32 (a host).
A line that is no address: the file keeps it as typed, lower-cased (the IP page refuses to save it); Core drops it and keeps the entry.
A bare address with no mask: the file keeps it, Core lists CIDRs only.
A mask written /08: the file keeps it, Core drops it as netip.ParsePrefix does.
0.0.0.0/0, below the lowest mask: the file keeps it, Core drops it.
A mask of /7, below /8: the file keeps it, Core drops it.
A mask of /33: the file keeps it, Core drops it.
An IPv6 CIDR in the IPv4 list: the file keeps it, Core drops it.

Invalid UTF-8 bytes in the list: the sanitizer turns the line into text that is no entry (what the file holds there depends on the PHP build, so the valid lines it holds are observed); the valid entries around it stay.
A NUL inside an entry: the sanitizer strips it, so the line is the entry again, repeated.
Stored text that is no base64: it decodes to bytes that hold no entry (the file holds garbage there, which depends on the PHP build: the valid lines it holds are observed).
An array where the text is stored: Core reads no entry. Not observed in today's PHP, which reads the array as the text Array (with a PHP warning).
One IPv6 entry.
Several IPv6 entries.
Entries with comments, blank lines and CRLF.
Upper-case hex: the decode lower-cases it, so the file and Core hold the lower-case entry.
The lowest mask, /32.
The highest mask, /128.
An address with a zone: the file keeps it, Core drops it.
A mask of /31, below /32: the file keeps it, Core drops it.
An IPv4 CIDR in the IPv6 list: the file keeps it, Core drops it.
An array where the text is stored: Core reads no entry. Not observed in today's PHP, which reads the array as the text Array (with a PHP warning).
An entry in each list: each is in its own file and projection.
